title: we built our tycoon's first version almost entirely with AI, heres what actually broke
author: Chaibi_Alaa
selftext:
first version of our city tycoon was basically all generative: blender plus meshy for the models, and a lot of bought asset packs on top to fill the gaps. it got us a playable map way faster than we could have modelled it by hand, thats not nothing and im not here to dunk on the tools.

what broke wasnt quality per asset. individually most of them were fine. the problem was that nothing belonged to the same world. every pack had its own scale, its own texel density, its own idea of how saturated a roof should be. put forty of those on one street and it reads as a catalogue, not a city. the old map was a grid of empty buildable plots in the middle, rectangular npc blocks round the edge, no grass, flat lighting. you could see every seam.

what we changed, roughly in order of how much it mattered:

\- artists on textures and art direction, so there's one rule for materials instead of forty

\- remodelled the map instead of patching it

\- moved the buildings onto our own procedural script, so a storefront gets generated to our spec instead of being found and fitted

\- and a design change that mattered as much as the art: we stopped building one map you replay a thousand times and went to real cities as stages

we still use generative tools, just earlier in the chain now: reference images while we're deciding what a building should look like, and tts for the rival voices. the generation moved from the final asset to the concept.

the thing i still dont have a good answer for: at what point in your own project did mixing generated and bought assets stop scaling? for us it fell apart somewhere around forty buildings on screen. curious whether thats a common wall or whether we just had bad asset hygiene.

comments.author: Chaibi_Alaa
comments.body: wider shot of the same old map for context, this is what i mean by a grid of empty plots with the npc blocks pushed out to the edge. the whole middle is buildable and completely inert.
